title: Fit4NUSS- Prehabilitation for patients prior to correction of congenital chest wall deformities
summary: Rehabilitation before surgery is called “prehabilitation”. It has been proven for many major operations that prehabilitation improves the surgical outcome more than rehabilitation alone and that patients have significantly fewer problems and pain after the operation, are more satisfied and recover more quickly without assistance. Such studies have not yet been carried out for patients with chest wall deformities, but a positive effect can be assumed. Fit4NUSS is intended to answer the question of whether 6 weeks of guided prehabilitation has a positive effect on the postoperative course, psychological well-being, mobilization, ability to work and exercise.

interventions.name:
Intervention group: patients under prehabilitation six weeks prior to 4 weeks after operation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adolescents and young adults with chest wall deformity (funnel or keel chest)
- Planned surgical correction of the chest wall deformity
- written informed consent of the legal guardian and the underage patient or written informed consent of the adult patient
Exclusion criteria:
- insufficient knowledge of German or English
- Other physical disabilities
- Pre-existing conditions with contraindications to physical exertion and sport
